originality.rationale: The exact same truncated local algebra is analyzed by Farooq, arXiv:2605.15670, but the result explicitly assumes characteristic zero and asserts square-zero operators; the accepted characteristic-two theorem produces rank-two nilpotent operators of exact index three, so that result cannot imply the new statement. Achar–Henderson, arXiv:0712.1079, covers orbit geometry of pairs consisting of a vector and a nilpotent matrix, but not the Rota–Baxter equations or their characteristic-dependent failure. Guo–Rosenkranz–Zheng, arXiv:1402.3702, classifies small semigroup algebras over characteristic-zero fields, not arbitrary embedding dimension in characteristic two. The indexed published-results searches produced no same-claim entry. The finite-field Gaussian terms and basic nilpotent orbit theory are acknowledged as known constituents; the new result is the operator-theoretic reduction, sharp modular index/dimension jump, and joint rank/index census. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a publication-priority guarantee.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated weight-zero Rota–Baxter equation develops a dense open family of exact nilpotency-index-three operators precisely in characteristic two for every embedding dimension at least two; no such operators exist in odd characteristic. The reduced parameter variety undergoes a dimension jump by floor(d/2), unbounded in d. Complete finite-field rank and square-index distributions supply a natural quantitative classification, beyond the previously established characteristic-zero operator classification and standalone nilpotent orbit counts.
